newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bond prices ease on cautious market.
newsitem.headline: Danish bond prices ease on cautious market.

text.p: Danish bond prices eased down on Friday, following U.S. treasuries, and dealers said that investors were likely to stay largely on the sidelines, watching Friday's German IFO data and next Tuesday's Humphrey Hawkins testimony by Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan.
"It has alll the signs of a waiting market," a dealer said.
At 0735 GMT the outgoing benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was down to 113.78, yielding 5.91 percent, from Thursday afternoon's 113.89.
Its successor from September 1, the seven percent 2007 bond, slipped 0.09 point to 106.57, yielding 6.11 percent.
The 2007 bond's spread to the 10-year German bund was 54 basis points, compared to Thursday's 55 bp.
The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 fell 0.40 point to 91.78.
The crown eased slightly, to 3.8090 to the mark from yesterday's 3.8085. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
